translationRepairs: In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, then served as a Grand Council clerk.
In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, serving as a Grand Council clerk.
充軍機章京 marks filling the Grand Council clerkship together with the Inner Cabinet secretaryship, not a later sequential posting implied by then.

Longer terms for governors-general and governors would lighten the tribute counties and districts must supply them; easing the routine charges imposed on local magistrates would allow more capable officials to survive in post."

If governors-general and governors served longer terms, counties and districts would have to supply their establishments less; if the routine charges against county and district magistrates were relaxed, more talented men could be preserved in office."
The original is ungrammatical and 供億 is the counties’ burden of supplying official establishments, which the replacement restores.

The Qin ruled through draconian law, measuring documents by the stone and scheduling work by the bushel; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.

The Qin ruled through draconian law, weighing documents by the stone and assigning them by quota; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.
衡石程書 is weighing documents by the stone and setting processing quotas, not scheduling work by the bushel.

In 1821 the Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors-general and governors, including Sun Yuting, proposed banning illicit surcharges on grain transport, formally capping collection at eighty percent while tacitly allowing an extra twenty percent.
江、浙督撫 names both governors-general and governors; governors alone drops 督.

Yet officials cannot control the people without wielding these three charges: licentiates and Imperial Academy students are temporarily stripped of status, ordinary commoners are detained, and release is requested only after they make up payment.
生監 is shengyuan and jiansheng, not specifically students who purchased degrees.

When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the ministries for deliberation.
下部議 is referring the memorial down to the ministries, not a single ministry deliberating on its own.

少詹事 is the junior supervisor of the heir apparent’s household, and 內閣學士 is a secretariat academician, not Grand Secretary 大學士.
He served successively as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
He served successively as Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and as a Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
The literal likewise names the wrong offices: 少詹事 is not a generic junior tutor and 內閣學士 is not Grand Secretary.

Ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji, he established the facts, secured the dismissal of Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun, and secured varying punishments for other offenders.

Ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji, he established the facts, secured the dismissal of Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun (then residing at home), and secured varying punishments for other offenders.
在籍按察使 is a judicial commissioner residing at his native place, not an acting 署 commissioner.

He was ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji; the facts were established, and he requested stripping Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun of office, with other offenders punished by military exile in varying degrees.

He was ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji; the facts were established, and he requested stripping Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun, then residing at home, of office, with other offenders punished by military exile in varying degrees.
在籍 is native-place residence, not acting office, but at-home as a preposed adjective is awkward; render 在籍 as then residing at home.

In 1838 he concurrently managed the affairs of the Shuntian Prefect and presided over the metropolitan examination.

He served in the Ministry of War, rose to vice director, presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination, and was appointed censor and supervising secretary.
遷員外郎 is promotion to vice director, not department director.

He also impeached Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, first listed among the six methods of capital-inspection dismissal yet who argued in person to be changed to third class, treating the process as a game; the Censor-in-Chief was severely censured while Se Cheng'e was still listed as ill.
列入六法 is the jingcha six-method dismissal list, not six punishments; 改列三等 is a change of listing, and 仍列有疾 keeps him listed as ill.

He also impeached Censorate capital-inspection Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, who had first been listed among the six punishments yet came in person to the public hall to argue, seeking to be changed to third class, treating the matter back and forth like child's play; the Censor-in-Chief was severely deliberated upon, yet Se Cheng'e was still listed as having illness.

He also impeached Censorate capital-inspection Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, who had first been listed among the six methods yet came in person to the public hall to argue, seeking to be changed to third class, treating the matter back and forth like child's play; the Censor-in-Chief was severely deliberated upon, yet Se Cheng'e was still listed as having illness.
六法 in this capital-inspection context is the six methods, not punishments.

He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fangshou, requesting they be referred to the governor for investigation and severe impeachment;
熊方受 is the personal name, but 請 governs 飭交撫臣查察嚴參 and is not a second 受請 charge; the proposed text restores the name then invents illicit solicitations.

He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fangshou, requesting they be referred to the governor for investigation and severe impeachment;
The name is 熊方受; 請 introduces the request that the governor investigate, so accepting bribes/solicitations is not in the sentence.

太常寺丞 is vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and 並罷之 reports the resulting dismissals rather than Engui personally dismissing them.
